headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: CrewAI can write broad filesystem and Goose can modify git and use MCP, creating dangerous default conflict, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, while Goose shares state via the filesystem and can consume files in the user filesystem. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge through files, even without a dedicated shared channel. The pathway is not provably blocked in either profile.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a file Goose later parses as instructions
IF Goose reads CrewAI-produced files without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate their working directories
Disable automatic file ingestion in Goose workflows
Add a provenance header to files passed between agents
Require manual review before Goose executes file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and Goose touches source code and files in cwd while sharing state via filesystem. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive file contents to the other, and Goose’s MCP/extensions broaden exfiltration paths. This is a default-config risk because neither profile shows isolation by default.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same workspace or cwd
IF either agent processes files containing secrets or proprietary source
mitigations: Use separate per-agent workspaces
Remove secrets from shared directories before running either agent
Restrict Goose extensions to approved MCP servers only
Run both agents under distinct OS users

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and Goose can also write the filesystem, modify git state, install packages, and use MCP. Their concurrency models explicitly allow shared state via filesystem, so concurrent writes and git mutations can collide in default setups. The blast radius includes irreversible repo corruption or conflicting package changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Goose modifies git state while CrewAI writes files concurrently
mitigations: Serialize access to the repo with a lock file
Assign each agent a separate checkout
Disable git-mutating actions for one agent during parallel runs
Snapshot the workspace before starting both agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew can emit synthesized outputs that Goose may treat as input for coding or ops actions, and Goose has tool authority including shell, git, and MCP. Because neither profile shows a verification gate between them, a bad CrewAI output can cascade into concrete actions by Goose. That is a dangerous default pathway with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF Goose consumes CrewAI output as authoritative task input
IF Goose is allowed to act on that output without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human approval step between agents
Require Goose to verify CrewAI claims against source files
Limit Goose to read-only mode for CrewAI-derived tasks
Log and diff all actions triggered from CrewAI outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, but CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys while Goose handles source code, files in cwd, and extension-specific tokens. If regulated data or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, differing retention and logging behavior can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent logs or retains those materials beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review each agent’s logging and retention settings before use
Use separate secret stores for each agent
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
